Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.

scenes.headline: Connect. Don't paste.
lines: Copying and pasting data into a chat goes stale the moment you do it.
A connector lets the agent read live data, and take real actions.

items: A snapshot, out of date in minutes

right.title: Connect the tool
items: Finds what it needs on its own

scenes.headline: MCP is one plug for every tool.

lines.say: The standard is called M C P, the Model Context Protocol.
lines.cap: The standard is called MCP, the Model Context Protocol.

lines: It gives the agent live data from your docs, tickets, and code.
It lets the agent take real actions, like creating, updating, and sending.
And it works the same way across harnesses.

scenes.headline: A name, a command, a key.
lines: Setting one up takes three things.
A name, and a command to start the server.
And a key. Keep the key in an environment variable. Never paste it into the file.

highlights.label: Key
highlights.note: The key comes from an env var

scenes.headline: Grant the least access that works.
lines: Give the least access that works.
Start read only.
Use scoped tokens.
And require approval for anything that writes or sends.

cards.d: Add write access later, on purpose
Kept in env vars, never in files
A human OKs anything that sends

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
MCP gives your agent live data and real actions, through one standard.
Your mission: connect one tool you use every day, read only, and ask the agent a question about it.
